brief:
Southern Lebanese residents are cautiously returning to their villages under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement between Israel and Lebanon. According to Mondoweiss, those who have come back have discovered their homes largely destroyed, with Israeli forces maintaining a daily presence across the occupied territory.

The returnees face the remnants of conflict: ruined structures, displaced lives, and the continued military occupation of their land. Residents describe an existence marked by uncertainty, as the fragile agreement holds while Israeli forces remain embedded in southern Lebanon.
dek: As part of a U.S.-brokered agreement with Israel and Lebanon, residents of some southern villages are cautiously returning to their homes. What they have found is a shell of their former lives, and a daily menacing presence of the Israeli occupation.
title: Returning Lebanese villagers find homes destroyed by Israeli occupation
